name: US recession risk
summary: US economy grew 3.4% in Q3; recession indicators quiet
state: The advance estimate on 29 Oct showed US GDP grew at a 3.4% annualised rate in Q3. The real-time Sahm rule indicator is 0.00, far from the 0.5 recession trigger, and the 10y–2y curve is positive at +0.38. October payrolls are the next test.
for_you: Recession risk in the US looks low for now. The main risk to growth is the combination of high energy prices and rising interest rates.
rubric_hit: Sahm rule indicator < 0.30 and no negative GDP quarter in the latest two releases.

sources.title: Axios — U.S. economy races ahead with 3.4% growth in third quarter

why: A US recession drags world trade, earnings and jobs; it is the single biggest swing factor for the global cycle.
drivers: Labour market, consumer spending, credit conditions, rates and fiscal policy.

rubric.alert: Sahm ≥ 0.50, or two consecutive negative GDP quarters, or NBER declares recession.
rubric.watch: Sahm 0.30–0.49, or one negative GDP quarter, or payrolls negative in a release.
rubric.normal: Sahm rule indicator < 0.30 and no negative GDP quarter in the latest two releases.
